lessons.title: Understand Percent
lessons.objective: I can explain a percent as a rate per 100, model it on a decimal grid or tape diagram, and interpret percents greater than 100%.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain what a percent means using the words per hundred, part, whole, and equivalent ratio.

concept.heading: What a percent really says
concept.intro: Percent means per hundred. Any part-to-whole comparison becomes a percent by rewriting it as an equivalent ratio whose second term is 100. A decimal grid makes that visible: 100 squares, one for each percent.
concept.keyIdea: Understanding Percent. Formula: Percent = Parts per 100 = Ratio of a number to 100. 1. Percent means 'per hundred' (% = /100). 2. On a 100-grid, each square represents 1% = 0.01 = 1/100. 3. Fraction to Percent: Scale fraction to a denominator of 100

worked.title: Watch me turn a vote into a percent
lines: Students voted on a mascot, and 4 out of every 10 voters chose the tiger. I want to know how many that is out of 100.
"4 out of every 10" is a ratio, so I write an equivalent ratio with 100 as the second term. Multiplying both terms by 10 gives 40 out of 100.
On a decimal grid of 100 squares, I shade 40 squares — one square for each percent.
40 out of 100 is written 40%. So 40% of the students voted for the tiger.
linesEs: Los estudiantes votaron por una mascota, y 4 de cada 10 votantes eligieron al tigre. Quiero saber cuántos son de cada 100.
«4 de cada 10» es una razón, así que escribo una razón equivalente con 100 como segundo término. Multiplicar los dos términos por 10 da 40 de cada 100.
En una cuadrícula decimal de 100 cuadros, sombreo 40 cuadros — un cuadro por cada porcentaje.
40 de cada 100 se escribe 40%. Entonces el 40% de los estudiantes votó por el tigre.
worked.titleEs: Mírame convertir una votación en un porcentaje

together.title: Let's do one together
lines: Shanice's gray kitten weighs 4 ounces. The orange kitten weighs 1.5 times as much. What percent of the gray kitten's weight is the orange kitten's weight?
The gray kitten is the whole, so its weight is 100%.
Draw a tape diagram: one full tape is 100%. The orange kitten needs 1.5 tapes — one whole tape plus half of another.
One whole is 100% and half a whole is 50%, so 100% + 50% = 150%. The orange kitten weighs 150% of the gray kitten's weight — more than one whole, which matches it being the heavier kitten.
linesEs: El gatito gris de Shanice pesa 4 onzas. El gatito naranja pesa 1.5 veces eso. ¿Qué porcentaje del peso del gatito gris es el peso del gatito naranja?
El gatito gris es el entero, así que su peso es el 100%.
Dibuja un diagrama de barras: una barra completa es el 100%. El gatito naranja necesita 1.5 barras — una barra entera más la mitad de otra.
Un entero es 100% y medio entero es 50%, así que 100% + 50% = 150%. El gatito naranja pesa el 150% del peso del gatito gris — más de un entero, lo que concuerda con que sea el gatito más pesado.

vocabulary.definition: A percent is a ratio that compares a number to 100, so every percent answers the question “how many out of 100?”
A ratio that compares a number to 100. The word means “per hundred,” and the symbol is %.
The meaning hidden inside the word percent: for every group of 100. It is why every percent can be written as a fraction over 100.
A 10-by-10 grid of 100 squares. Shading squares shows a percent directly, one square per percent.
A comparison of one part against the whole amount. In a percent, the whole is always 100%.
vocabulary.example: The whole = 100%; the part = the percent

vocabulary.definition: More than one whole. A percent above 100 means the amount is larger than the thing it is being compared to.
vocabulary.example: 150% of the gray kitten = 1.5 times its weight

vocabulary.definition: A ratio with the same value, made by multiplying or dividing both terms by the same number.
A bar split into equal parts to show a percent.

lessons.title: Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
lessons.objective: I can write equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents for the same value.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my conversions using the words percent, decimal, equivalent, and benchmark.

concept.heading: How can one value be written as a fraction, a decimal, AND a percent?
concept.intro: Equivalent forms name the same value in different ways. Percent means "out of 100," so a fraction is already a percent once its denominator is 100.
concept.keyIdea: Fraction, Decimal & Percent Equivalence. 1. Percent to Decimal: Divide by 100 (move decimal point 2 places left). 2. Decimal to Percent: Multiply by 100 (move decimal point 2 places right). 3. Fraction to Percent: Divide numerator by denominator, then convert decimal to percent

worked.title: Watch me
lines: A player scored 3/4 of the points. Percent means out of 100, so I want an equivalent fraction with 100 on the bottom.
What do I multiply the denominator 4 by to get 100? 4 × 25 = 100, so my scale factor is 25.
I have to multiply the top by that same 25: 3 × 25 = 75. So 3/4 = 75/100.
75 out of 100 is 75%. And 75/100 as a decimal is 0.75, because hundredths sit two places after the point.
So 3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75 = 75%. All three name the same score.
linesEs: Un jugador anotó 3/4 de los puntos. Porcentaje significa de cada 100, así que quiero una fracción equivalente con 100 abajo.
¿Por cuánto multiplico el denominador 4 para llegar a 100? 4 × 25 = 100, así que mi factor de escala es 25.
Tengo que multiplicar el numerador por ese mismo 25: 3 × 25 = 75. Entonces 3/4 = 75/100.
75 de cada 100 es 75%. Y 75/100 como decimal es 0.75, porque las centésimas están dos lugares después del punto.
Entonces 3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75 = 75%. Las tres formas nombran el mismo puntaje.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's change 1/5 into a fraction out of 100, then a decimal and a percent.
What do we multiply the denominator 5 by to get 100? (20)
Now multiply the numerator by that same 20: 1 × 20 = ? (20) So 1/5 = 20/100.
20 out of 100 is what percent? (20%) And as a decimal? (0.2)
linesEs: Convirtamos 1/5 en una fracción de cada 100, y luego en decimal y porcentaje.
¿Por cuánto multiplicamos el denominador 5 para llegar a 100? (20)
Ahora multiplica el numerador por ese mismo 20: 1 × 20 = ? (20) Entonces 1/5 = 20/100.
¿20 de cada 100 es qué porcentaje? (20%) ¿Y como decimal? (0.2)

support.prompt: What does the word percent mean?
support.explanation: Percent means per hundred, which is why every percent can be written as a fraction with a denominator of 100.
feedback: Per ten would be a tenth, not a percent.
Per thousand is a different comparison entirely.
"Part" does not say how big the whole is; a percent always compares to 100.
hints: Look at the second half of the word: cent.
A century is 100 years; a cent is 1/100 of a dollar.
Percent = per 100.

support.prompt: 3 out of every 10 students walk to school. What percent is that?
support.explanation: Multiply both terms of the ratio by 10 to compare to 100: 3 out of 10 becomes 30 out of 100, or 30%.
feedback: 3 out of 100 would be 3%, but the ratio here is out of 10.
10 is the second term of the original ratio, not the percent.
That adds the two numbers instead of scaling the ratio.
hints: A percent compares to 100, so rewrite the ratio out of 100.
What do you multiply 10 by to get 100?
Multiply BOTH terms by that same number.

support.prompt: A decimal grid has 100 squares and 65 are shaded. What percent is shaded?
support.explanation: Each square is one percent, so 65 shaded squares is 65%.
feedback: This is ten times too small — moving the decimal one extra place shrinks the real percent down to this.
35 is the number of UNshaded squares.
100% would mean every square is shaded.
hints: How many squares are in the whole grid?
Each square stands for 1%.
Count the shaded squares.

support.prompt: Which percent means MORE than one whole?
support.explanation: 100% is exactly one whole, so any percent above 100 is more than one whole.
feedback: 0.8% is a tiny sliver of one whole.
80% is less than one whole.
100% is exactly one whole, not more.
hints: What percent stands for one whole?
Anything above that is more than the whole.
Compare each choice to 100.

steps: Setup: 7 out of every 10 seats are taken. What percent is that?
Step 3: So 7% of the seats are taken.
support.explanation: Step 2 keeps the number but changes the whole. To compare to 100, multiply BOTH terms by 10: 7 out of 10 becomes 70 out of 100, so 70% of the seats are taken.
hints: Does 7 out of 10 mean mostly full or mostly empty?
What must you multiply 10 by to get 100?
Do the same thing to the 7.

feedback: Try again: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 as well.
Build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 — multiply the top and bottom by the same number.
hints: Percent means out of 100. What do you multiply the denominator 5 by to get 100?
5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the numerator by that same 20 to build the equivalent fraction.
3 × 20 = 60, so 3/5 = 60/100. A fraction out of 100 IS the percent.

feedback: Scale 7/20 up to a denominator of 100 first.
Double-check: 20 × 5 = 100, so the top must be multiplied by 5 too.
hints: The denominator 20 is friendly: 20 × 5 = 100, and percents are always 'out of 100'.
Make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 by multiplying top AND bottom by the same number.
Multiply 7/20 by 5/5: the bottom becomes 100. Whatever the top becomes is your percent.

support.explanation: 45% means 45/100, and 45/100 written as a decimal is 0.45 (forty-five hundredths).
feedback: 0.045 is forty-five THOUSANDTHS — one place too far. Percent to decimal moves the point exactly two places left.
Divide the percent by 100, or move the decimal point left 2 places.
45.0 keeps the percent's full size. Percent means 'per hundred,' so the decimal form must be much smaller — move the point two places left.
hints: Percent means 'out of 100', so 45% is the fraction 45/100.
To turn a percent into a decimal, divide by 100 — the decimal point slides two places to the LEFT.
Start at 45. and move the decimal two places left: 45 → 4.5 → where does it land after the second hop?

support.explanation: 0.75 = 75/100. Simplify by dividing both by 25: 75÷25 = 3 and 100÷25 = 4. So 0.75 = 3/4.
feedback: Try converting the decimal to a fraction with 100 in the denominator.
Think: 0.75 = 75/100. Can you simplify that fraction?
hints: 0.75 is read 'seventy-five hundredths' — the place value tells you the denominator.
Write the decimal as a fraction over 100, then simplify by dividing top and bottom by a common factor.
Write 75/100, then divide both the 75 and the 100 by 25 to simplify.

steps: Read the digits as the percent: The numerator is 3 and the denominator is 5, so the student writes 35%.
support.explanation: You cannot just read the digits. Percent means out of 100, so build the equivalent fraction: 5 × 20 = 100, and 3 × 20 = 60. So 3/5 = 60/100 = 0.6 = 60%, not 35%.
hints: Do the digits 3 and 5 tell you how many parts out of 100?

support.prompt: Predict the shaded amount for these settings.  Round to four decimal places if needed.
support.explanation: 35% of 100 = 35. 35% = 0.35 = 7/20. The hundred grid always shows the percentage; the whole amount can change.

core.prompt: The orange kitten weighs 1.5 times as much as the gray kitten. What percent of the gray kitten's weight is that?
core.explanation: The gray kitten is the whole, or 100%. One and a half wholes is 100% + 50% = 150%.
feedback: 1.5% is a tiny sliver — but the orange kitten is heavier.
15% would be a small fraction of the gray kitten, not more than all of it.
50% is only half the gray kitten's weight.
hints: Which kitten is the whole?
One whole is 100%. What is half a whole?
Add the whole and the half.

steps: Setup: A player scored 150% of the weekly goal of 200 points.
Step 1: 150% is more than one whole.
Step 2: So the player scored 150 points.
Step 3: The player beat the 200-point goal.
core.explanation: Step 2 reads the percent as if it were the points themselves. A percent is a comparison, not an amount: 150% of 200 points is 1.5 × 200 = 300 points.
hints: Steps 1 and 3 are both right — check Step 2.
150% of what?

core.prompt: A game shows your score as 7/8 complete. What percent is that?
core.explanation: 8 does not scale to 100 by a whole number, so divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, and 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. That is 87.5 out of 100.
feedback: Convert the fraction to a decimal first.
8 will not scale to 100 evenly — divide 7 by 8, then multiply by 100.
88% is the rounded version, but this score converts exactly. Divide 7 by 8 and keep every decimal place — the percent is not a whole number.
hints: Try the out-of-100 move first: is there a whole number you can multiply 8 by to get exactly 100?
There isn't (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), so use the backup method: divide the numerator by the denominator.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, which is 87.5/100 — slide the decimal two places right to read the percent.

steps: Divide the bottom by the top: 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6
core.explanation: The student divided in the wrong order. To turn a fraction into a decimal, divide the TOP by the bottom: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, then × 100 → 62.5%. So 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. (A check: 5/8 is less than 1, so the percent must be under 100%, never 160%.)
hints: Is 5/8 more or less than one whole? Then can its percent be over 100%?
8 will not scale to 100 evenly, so divide the numerator by the denominator: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, which is 62.5/100 → 62.5%.

steps: Setup: Which is larger: 40% of 200, or 150% of 40?
Step 2: So 150% of 40 must be the larger amount.
stretch.explanation: Step 2 compares the percents instead of the amounts. Each percent applies to a different whole: 40% of 200 = 80, while 150% of 40 = 60. Since 80 > 60, the first amount is larger — even though its percent is smaller.
hints: What is each percent a percent OF?
Compute both amounts before comparing.

stretch.prompt: A car dealership sold 50 cars last month: 20 sedans, 15 SUVs, 10 trucks, and 5 vans. The owner will order 100 cars for next month and wants the order to match last month's sales pattern. Write each type as a percent, then say how many of each to order — and explain why percents make this easier than the raw counts.
stretch.explanation: Each count is out of 50, so multiply both terms by 2 to compare to 100: sedans 20/50 = 40/100 = 40%, SUVs 15/50 = 30/100 = 30%, trucks 10/50 = 20/100 = 20%, vans 5/50 = 10/100 = 10%. The percents total 100%, which confirms the whole is accounted for. Because the new order is exactly 100 cars, each percent IS the number to order: 40 sedans, 30 SUVs, 20 trucks, and 10 vans. Percents make this easier because they restate every count against the same whole of 100, so two months with different totals can be compared directly.
hints: Each sale count is out of 50 — rewrite each one out of 100.
What do you multiply 50 by to get 100?
Check that your four percents add to 100%.
2 ÷ 3 doesn't terminate — is 0.67 the exact decimal?
0.67 is rounded. The precise decimal is 0.666... (repeating), making the percent 66.7% or 66⅔%.

stretch.prompt: A student says 3/8 is greater than 40% because 3 and 8 are bigger numbers than 4 and 0. Is the student correct? Convert both values to the same form and explain.
stretch.frame: The student is ___ because 3/8 = ___ = ___%, which is ___ than 40%.
stretch.explanation: Bigger-looking digits do not mean a bigger value — the two amounts have to be in the same form before you compare them. Converting the fraction gives 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375, which is 37.5%. Since 37.5% is less than 40%, the student is not correct: 3/8 is the smaller value.
hints: Bigger digits do NOT mean a bigger value — 3/8 and 40% can only be compared in the same form.
You can put 40% in fraction form instantly — it is 40/100. Now get 3/8 out of 100: check whether 8 scales to 100 by a whole number.
8 does not scale to 100, so divide: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 = 37.5/100 = 37.5%. Compare that with 40/100.
